scope: Proposition 2.6 (Target flattening) of the manuscript “Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for p>2” (preprints/Strong-diffeomorphic-approximation-in-three-dimensions-for-p-gt-2-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 368 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 824a96588feb42d5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 12-13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Given ε > 0, 0 < λ < 1/100, and a positive continuous fine tolerance a on Λ, one can retain a compact set K ⊂ D with µ(D \ K) < ε and construct a Lipschitz map S0 : Λ → Λ with the following properties. 1. The map is the identity outside finitely many disjoint rectangular boxes compactly contained in Λ, Lip(S0) ≤ C, and |S0(y) − y| < a(y). The constant C is absolute. For 0 < κ ≤ 1, Sκ = (1 − κ)S0 + κ id is a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of Λ onto itself. 2. With Fκ = Sκ ◦ f for 0 ≤ κ ≤ 1, |DFκ| ≤ C|Df| a.e. on Ω, |DFκ − Df| ≤ Cλ|Df| a.e. on K. (2.7) Moreover, Fκ → F0 strongly in W1,p(Ω; R3), and rank DF0 = rank Df almost everywhere on K. 3. The compact set F0(K) is contained in finitely many compact flat plate patches with pairwise disjoint ambient neighborhoods. Each patch lies in a plane of slope at most Cλ in one of the chosen coordinates. Each patch has an assigned rank, either one or two; the rank-one patches can in addition retain any prescribed small directional grouping of im Df. 4. There is a compact zero-volume set Z ⋐ Λ, contained in finitely many piecewise affine graph sheets, such that S0 : Λ \ S−1 0 (Z) −→ Λ \ Z (2.8) 12 is a locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism. Its only non-singleton fibres are the collapsed vertical intervals over points of Z. Consequently F0 is a homeomorphism from Ω \ F−1 0 (Z) onto Λ \ Z. For almost every target point outside Z, its unique preimage under this last homeomorphism either is a regular point of F0 with positive invertible differential and the power-mean test in (2.1), or belongs to a fixed source null set. When p ≥ 3, the second alternative occurs only on a target null set.
